artifacts.notes: Whole 1,162-page PDF scan, registered remote because no project consumer needs the 51,720,493-byte payload. Internet Archive metadata reports 1,164 viewer images; at every checked locus the viewer leaf n maps to PDF artifact page n+1. Thus viewer n12 is artifact p. 13, n711-n712 are pp. 712-713, n714-n715 are pp. 715-716, and n1108-n1110 are pp. 1109-1111. Printed pagination is recorded independently on each passage. The OCR is a finding aid only: bounded absence and wording/content claims were verified against page images, not inferred from failed OCR searches.
artifacts.rights_basis: The underlying book was first published at Tours in 1922, before the pre-1931 United States public-domain line applicable in 2026. Its maximum possible United States term expired before URAA restoration, so there was no subsisting term to restore on 1 January 1996. The PDF is a faithful mechanical page reproduction of that public-domain book; its machine-produced image and OCR layers add no human authorship. This conclusion relies on publication date and the mechanical character of the reproduction, not on Internet Archive availability, successful retrieval, or a host licence label.

artifacts.notes: One header and three data rows, each on exactly one physical LF-delimited line; columns seq, element_key, printed_page, ia_leaf, latin, notes. Source order is seq 1 Munda cor meum, seq 2 Per evangelica dicta, seq 3 Dominus sit in corde meo. These are Mame source rows, not the Cummiskey rows and not target-edition editorial projections. The Munda full-print rubric names the deacon and the next page explicitly reuses that prayer for the priest without sacred ministers; no unconditional actor field is asserted in this artifact. The three bounded passage records control exact TSV physical lines without duplicating a text payload.

The source Mame spelling, ligatures, accents, capitals and pointing are retained, with no reading or pointing supplied from the 1962 target or another witness.

edition.authority: Licensed commercial printing conformed to the Vatican typical edition, not a typical edition and not a new promulgating station. The approval leaf states that the Missal was examined against the Vatican edition and the decrees of 24 October 1920 and 26 October 1921, and Albertus Negre, Archbishop of Tours, approved it at Tours on 17 May 1922.
